follow-up time: Until subsequent live birth or study end
exposure: Vaginal delivery complicated by shoulder dystocia
cohort: 46,162 women with a first live birth at Aarhus University Hospital, Denmark, between 1989 and 2010
finding: The impact of mode of delivery on subsequent birth rate and time to next birth was minimal, with the greatest reduction observed among women with assisted vaginal delivery complicated by shoulder dystocia.
mod_finding: Women with any type of caesarean had a 6% reduction in the rate of subsequent live birth, which did not vary by type (emergency or elective).
